objectives: Understand basics of High Energy Physics, also called Particle Physics. Special emphasis is on experimental break-through discoveries, but key theory ideas are also covered. Rather than technical details, the objective is to share the excitement of the quest for fundamental laws of physics.
content:
[Week 1 - 7] Part I. Overview and Discoveries in the 1st half of 20th century
........0) Overview of this course
........1) The origins of particle physics - atom, X-ray, electron, proton, positron, neutron
........2) Muon and pion
........3) Strangeness
........4) Antibaryons
........5) Resonances

[Week 8] Midterm Exam

[Week 9 - 15] Part 2. Discoveries in the third quarter of the 20th century
........6) Weak interactions
........7) Neutral kaon system,
........8) Structure of nucleon
........9) J/psi, tau, charm,

[Week 16] Final Exam

Note: This course will be continued to the next semester as "PH4066 Introduction to Particle Physics". The next semester will cover more recent discoveries in the last quarter of the 20th century and the 1st quarter of 21st century, including, 10. Quarks, gluons, jets, 11. Fifth quark, 12. Weak vector bosons, 13. Standard Model, 14. Top quark, 15. Mixing and CP violation in heavy quark mesons, 16, Neutrino masses and oscillations, 17. Open questions and cosmic connections.
books: Reference: "The Experimental Foundation of Particle Physics (Second Edition)" by Robert Cahn and Gerson Goldhaber
